description: We are Two Baldies Problem, a Barcelona-based team tackling the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge.
summary: A browser-based tool that helps explore lunar sites and screen them for Sun and Earth visibility using NASA open data.
details:
OrbitPass is a browser-based tool for exploring the Moon in 3D and screening lunar sites using NASA open data. It covers the south-pole rims, CLPS targets and Apollo sites, and users can also click the surface to pick a custom point.

What it does

  • Simulates 30 days of hourly Sun and Earth visibility per site, with the percentage of time each is visible and the longest dark period.
  • Computes a 360° terrain horizon from the LOLA elevation model, with a spherical-horizon fallback when terrain tiles are unavailable.
  • Compares its built-in ephemeris against NASA JPL Horizons.
  • Offers site comparison, an operating-window finder, a risk screening report and a first-person terrain walker.
  • Includes a professional view with mission tools, a mission manifest and curated NASA resources.

NASA data used
NASA Moon Trek (LRO WAC mosaic and LOLA DEM), JPL Horizons, and LROC NAC terrain data for Shackleton.

How it is built
HTML, JavaScript (ES modules) and three.js, served by nginx in Docker, which proxies and caches NASA tiles and the Horizons API. The source code is MIT-licensed.

Limitations
Results are approximate screening values and are not for landing safety or real mission planning. The elevation raster resolves about 0.67 km, and its encoding has not been independently validated.

Use of Super Intelligence
AI tools (large language models) were used for coding, debugging, code review and documentation.
